 New York (WRGB) — As federal cuts to food assistance ripple across the country, New York is moving to keep a lifeline in place for families who depend on free school meals.
 Gov. Hochul announced New York State will continue to fully fund its universal free school meals program. The state’s commitment is aimed at protecting about 2.5 million free school meals served each school day and helping families save up to $1,600 per child per year on groceries.
 PREVIOUS COVERAGE 
 The announcement comes after new reports this past week indicated other states are seeing declines in free school meal participation tied to federal cuts and changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP . New York officials say the state’s fully funded universal meals program will prevent schools from losing the funding needed to continue providing free meals.
 Gov. Hochul said,
 It’s shameful that President Trump and Washington Republicans are trying to take free school meals away from our kids – and that’s why I took action to ensure kids across New York won’t lose access to the free school meals they rely on. While Trump keeps finding new ways to raise costs for hardworking families, I’ll never stop fighting to protect our kids and help New Yorkers keep more money in their pockets. New York’s universal free school meals program was enacted by Hochul last year and is designed to ensure 2.7 million students statewide have access to free school breakfast and lunch. The law requires all school districts, charter schools and nonpublic schools that participate in the national school lunch and breakfast program to provide free breakfast and lunch to all students, regardless of family income.
 In the New York State FY27 Enacted Budget, Hochul secured a $395 million statewide investment in universal free school meals, an increase of $55 million above the previous fiscal year. State officials say that increased state funding means federal cuts to food assistance will not result in any New York schools receiving less funding for free meals, and that no New York student would lose access.
 With about 2.5 million free meals served per school day, state officials estimate schools across New York have already served about 75 million free school meals since the current school year started in September.
 Children in households that participate in SNAP and Medicaid are directly certified for free school meals. Families not enrolled in SNAP or Medicaid can still apply. More information on eligibility and how to apply is available at https://www.cn.nysed.gov .
 Assemblymember Jessica González-Rojas called the program essential for families and students.
 Universal free school meals is an issue I care deeply about, and I fought to make this legislation a reality because no child should go hungry and no family should have to struggle to put food on the table. As a mother, I know how important it is to make sure our children have what they need to learn, grow, and thrive. I am proud that we fought for and won universal free school meals in New York, and I applaud Governor Hochul for fully funding the program and protecting it from the Trump administration’s cruel cuts to food assistance. At a time when families are being squeezed by the rising cost of groceries, this investment puts money back in parents’ pockets and ensures millions of children can count on a nutritious breakfast and lunch at school. Feeding our children is a responsibility we all share, and I will never stop fighting to make sure no child is left behind. Trending
